evals.name: desktop-ops-direction-smoke
evals.prompt: I am designing a desktop operations app for finance analysts. It needs to feel calm and precise instead of flashy. Give me the design direction, the taste axes, and the main layout rules.
evals.expected_output: Gives a calm, precise direction and the requested taste axes, adapting layout and states for dense desktop work without requiring a named style family.

assertions.text: Response defines the taste axes before discussing decorative details
Agent reads references/platform-adaptation.md for desktop-specific guidance

evals.name: redesign-existing-dashboard-edge
evals.prompt: Our existing dashboard has too many floating cards, weak table hierarchy, and loading states that feel unfinished. I do not want a full redesign from zero. Tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Uses the critique workflow, prioritizes hierarchy and state fixes before styling, and avoids proposing a ground-up rewrite.

assertions.text: Response prioritizes hierarchy, layout, and state model before polish changes

evals.name: logo-only-negative
evals.prompt: I need a logo mark and mascot illustration for a new coffee brand. Help me craft the visual concept.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the task is outside the scope of this interface-design skill and does not overapply screen-layout guidance.

assertions.text: Does not frame the task as a web, app, or desktop interface problem

evals.name: motion-and-state-disclosure
evals.prompt: The onboarding flow looks polished when static, but hover, focus, loading, and error states still feel cheap. Where should I focus?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the interaction and state guidance, emphasizing state completeness before decorative motion.

assertions.text: Response treats state design as higher priority than extra animation

evals.name: bold-mixed-style-product-keeps-accessibility
evals.prompt: Design one dark project-planning screen for our creative studio. Mix editorial serif headlines with a dense neon-accented task board, a decorative gradient, and a playful animated flourish on completion. This is a one-off concept, not a design system; skip the taste-axis worksheet. Keyboard navigation and reduced-motion support matter.
evals.expected_output: Develops the requested mixed, expressive direction without imposing a restrained product style or system work. Keeps readable hierarchy, accessible contrast, keyboard focus, and a reduced-motion alternative.

assertions.text: Retains the dark canvas, serif and dense-board combination, decorative gradient, and completion flourish as coherent design choices rather than rejecting them by style rule
Includes legible text and controls, visible keyboard focus, and a reduced-motion alternative that preserves completion feedback
Does not require all five taste axes, a named style family, or a token system for this one-off concept

evals.name: critique-heuristics-are-not-quotas
evals.prompt: Critique a dense monitoring view with six equally important service panels. Operators must compare them, and all labels are required. Keep our expressive dark visual identity. Is it a failure if the whole view takes more than two seconds to understand, and must we remove 20% of the chrome?
evals.expected_output: Explains that glance and removal tests are diagnostic aids, not quotas. Evaluates comparison, grouping, readability, and states without forcing a hero or indiscriminate deletion.

assertions.text: Does not impose a two-second comprehension gate, 20% removal quota, or single dominant service panel
Preserves required labels and visual identity while proposing checks for service comparison, contrast, and status meaning beyond color alone

evals.name: platform-guidance-conflict-proposes-sourced-correction
evals.prompt: In our web app, matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches is true, but our decorative CSS animation still runs. The skill tells us to respect reduced motion without saying how. Check the browser/platform guidance, recommend a fix, and suggest a canonical skill clarification with a test. Do not edit installed copies.
evals.expected_output: Checks current browser/platform documentation, explains how application styles must respond to the preference, and proposes a sourced canonical clarification with a concrete reduced-motion check without silently changing installed copies.

assertions.text: Uses current official evidence for the disputed behavior, or explicitly reports unavailable evidence without asserting a verified resolution
Proposes a sourced canonical correction and a reproducible interaction check; does not mutate installed copies
